d: The serum hCG level, up to about 3,500 mIU/mL in current guidance, above which a normal intrauterine gestational sac should be visible on transvaginal ultrasound.
A positive pregnancy test with no pregnancy seen inside or outside the uterus on transvaginal ultrasound; serial hCG measurements and repeat imaging resolve it.

An autoimmune thrombophilia with lupus anticoagulant, anticardiolipin or anti-beta-2-glycoprotein I antibodies that causes thrombosis and recurrent pregnancy loss; in pregnancy it is treated with low-dose aspirin and heparin.
A stain for a maternally expressed, paternally imprinted gene product; it is negative in a complete mole, which has no maternal chromosomes, and positive in a partial mole.
Malignant trophoblastic disease, including invasive mole, choriocarcinoma and placental site trophoblastic tumor, recognized by a plateauing or rising hCG and usually cured with chemotherapy.

Two concentric echogenic rings around an early gestational sac, from the decidua parietalis and decidua capsularis, which supports an intrauterine pregnancy; the pseudosac of an ectopic pregnancy has only a single ring.

Chorionic villi swollen by fluid into vesicles with central acellular cisterns, the grape-like change of a hydatidiform mole; they are diffuse in a complete mole and mixed with normal villi in a partial mole.
